zh_summary: Warns that the Roadster unveil would be met with indifference by $TSLA investors ($TSLA -3.1% vs NDX -2.3%). Expected financial impact only +$.06/share incremental eps in 2029 (+1.1% of consensus 2029 adj eps of $5.40). Halo effect limited as few care about 0-60 under 1s or flying. en_summary: Warns that the Roadster unveil would be met with indifference by $TSLA investors ($TSLA -3.1% vs NDX -2.3%). Expected financial impact only +$.06/share incremental eps in 2029 (+1.1% of consensus 2029 adj eps of $5.40). Halo effect limited as few care about 0-60 under 1s or flying. TSLA always sells on the news. Remains cautious on $TSLA due to extended valuation, expected negative revisions, and view that unsupervised autonomy becomes commoditized.
text: I warned everyone that the Roadster unveil would be met with indifference by TSLA investors  ($TSLA -3.1% vs NDX -2.3%). One, while the engineering and tech were dazzling, the expected financial impact (we estimate +$.06/share incremental eps in 2029) is only +1.1% of consensus 2029 adj eps of $5.40. Second, the halo effect on the $TSLA franchise is likely to be limited since only a tiny subset of U.S. drivers care about going from 0-60 in under 1 second, or that the vehicle can fly short distances while doing flips mid-air.  Third, TSLA always sells on the news after its events and the same principle applies today.  We remain cautious on $TSLA due to its extended valuation, continued expected negative revisions, and our view that unsupervised autonomy becomes commoditized.

zh_summary: @scottmelker: Bank of America got only a $1.2B fine for money laundering failings while CZ served prison time for a lesser offense. $BAC
en_summary: @scottmelker: Bank of America got only a $1.2B fine for money laundering failings while CZ served prison time for a lesser offense. $BAC
text:
Bank of America only gets a $1.2B fine for money laundering failings, while CZ served prison time for a lesser offense

"Bank of America hit with $1.2 billion fine for money laundering failings. First of all, Elizabeth Warren, who I rarely agree with, wrote a tweet that was like, why isn't anybody in jail? I agree with her."

"They take your money in the fees, and they pay them to the government when they get in trouble. This was Chinese money laundering, one of the worst things you can possibly do. $5 billion that people know about, probably a lot more, and they only get a $1.2 billion fine, and nobody goes to jail."

"Meanwhile, CZ goes to jail in the United States for lesser crimes than the ones that are transparently being enacted by our very own banks, and nobody blinks an eye."

"This is why we Bitcoin. This is why we built DeFi. This is why crypto and blockchain were created."

"Biggest bank fines and settlements since 2000. This is only in this millennium. Bank of America has paid $88 billion in fines for money laundering and actual crimes. JP Morgan, $40 billion. UBS, $32 billion. Wells Fargo, $28 billion. Citigroup, $27 billion."

"How do these entities continue to exist paying fines for criminal activity this large? It's absolutely astounding."

name: Deepak Shenoy
zh_summary: @deepakshenoy suggests the RBI sell gold from its 660 tons to Indian gold ETFs and keep it in its vaults, buying back on redemptions; this would be cheaper and reduce FX demand from gold imports.
en_summary: @deepakshenoy suggests the RBI sell gold from its 660 tons to Indian gold ETFs and keep it in its vaults, buying back on redemptions; this would be cheaper and reduce FX demand from gold imports.
text:
Interesting proposal. I believe it will help if rbi effectively sells gold to the etfs and sequesters them in its vaults. So if rbi have 660 tons of gold and etfs want 10 tons, rbi can sell it to them and mark it as such in the rbi vault. 

It will be cheaper and then rbi can always purchase the gold back when there is a redemption. This will also reduce total money in the system since rbi sells and takes out money from the system. 

Eventually it still has custody of the gold, doesn't have to worry about losing access to gold (it can always buy it back) and etf demand is totally fulfilled and safe. 

It will hurt gold vaults to some extent cos we will trust rbi vaults far more than private ones. It will reduce some physical import demand perhaps as etfs own about 120 tons of gold this far but it's growing. Rbi has 660.

My suggestion was that rbi sells gold to jewellers but this does something equivalent and probably better.
